questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Given a Graph
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062030/assets/6c70d5f15424c4d7d67a3998a785a214e46e8dfa47b83839fd99a574b2f756cf.png)

The graph of the function $f(x)$, which is defined on $[-1,6]$, is shown above. It consists of three line segments and the arc of the semi-circle centered at $(4,0)$ with radius $1.$ Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[0,5].$
questions.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =3+\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5-0}\cdot (3+\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}+\frac{\pi }{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Over a Given Interval
questions.problem: What is the average value of $h(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x$ on the interval $[\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{2}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}h(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{4})}\,{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }\,{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }{(\frac{1}{2})(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})] \\  & =-\frac{2}{\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =-\frac{2}{\pi }(-1-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding an Interval Given the Average Value of a Function
questions.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=3-2x$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(3-2x)\,\text{d}x \\ 1 & ={\frac{1}{c}(3x-{x}^{2})|}_{0}^{c} \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{c}[(3c-{c}^{2})-(0)] \\ 1 & =3-c \\ -2 & =-c \\ c & =2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Over a Given Interval
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi -0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{8}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We calculate this integral using a substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{8}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{-1}{u}^{8}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{\frac{1}{\pi }(\frac{{u}^{9}}{9})|}_{1}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9\pi }[(-1)^{9}-{1}^{9}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{9\pi }(-2) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062030/assets/8ddd8493662174e0ddaf9bdd63b0ec382f6bb25c9079f1a339b71400b8cf3860.png)

The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-6,6],$ is shown above. The areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $15$, $60$ and $9,$ respectively (from left to right). 

Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[-6,6].$ Do not round the answer.

${f}_{\text{avg}}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Here, we see that

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-15+60-9=36.
$$

So, applying the average value formula, we find that the average value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6-(-6)}\cdot (36) \\  & =\frac{36}{12} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
